batch11.title: Batch FAISS face queries and resolve shared gallery identities together
batch11.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained search performance improvement.

## What has been done
A multi-face ANN search currently calls FAISS once per face and repeats gallery-name lookups for identities shared by those faces. This serializes independent HNSW queries and adds database round trips.

Submit the face embeddings as one FAISS query matrix, then resolve the unique matched identities together through the database adapter's existing lookup method. Preserve per-face result order, empty matches, thresholds, missing-neighbor filtering, requested limits, and facial-area metadata.

## How to test
Added real FAISS/SQLite integration coverage for normalized and unnormalized embeddings, verification and similarity searches, single and multiple faces, default and explicit limits, missing neighbors, empty batches, and shared identities. The numerical and returned-record results are compared with individual face searches.

[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43858024543) on Python 3.10 and 3.12:
- Original production source: 13 regression failures and 15 passing controls.
- Updated source, including the adjacent FAISS missing-neighbor, face-order, and SQLite suites: 48 passed in each environment.
- Repository-pinned Pylint: 10.00/10; MyPy: 145 source files passed; test formatting passed.

The same run measures a real FAISS 1.16.0 HNSW index with 10,000 128-dimensional vectors, 128 query faces, k=20, and two FAISS threads. Across seven repeated complete datastore searches, median time changed from 36.42 to 22.23 ms on Python 3.10 and from 29.94 to 17.87 ms on Python 3.12. These measurements use precomputed synthetic embeddings and an actual SQLite gallery; they exclude face detection and neural inference. No timing threshold is asserted in the regression tests.

batch12.title: Batch detected face embeddings during verification
batch12.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained verification performance improvement.

## What has been done
Verification currently calls representation separately for every detected face, even though representation already supports batched inference. A group photo therefore launches the recognition model repeatedly with singleton inputs.

Pass the already-extracted face crops to representation together, once per input image. Keep the original face order, BGR conversion, normalization, facial-area metadata, scalar custom-distance callbacks, and empty-face behavior. Check every anti-spoofing verdict before running that image's recognition batch.

## How to test
[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43859782785), Python 3.10 and 3.12:
- Original production source: 11 regression failures and 14 passing controls.
- Patched source plus the existing threshold, angular-distance, and empty-representation suites: 93 passed in each environment.
- Pylint 2.15.10: 10.00/10; MyPy 1.14.1: 145 source files passed; new-test formatting passed.

The new tests cover single and multiple faces, all four built-in metrics and a scalar custom metric, two normalization modes, best-match facial areas, empty extraction, precomputed embeddings, and a spoof later in the detected face list.

A separate case loads the real pretrained FaceNet ONNX weights and compares eight-face results with individual representations. With two CPU inference threads and five measured repetitions, recognition/preprocessing median time changed from 103.12 to 79.35 ms on Python 3.10 / ONNX Runtime 1.23.2 and from 72.90 to 63.26 ms on Python 3.12 / ONNX Runtime 1.32.0. Model forward calls changed from eight singleton calls to one batch. The observed embeddings were identical in these runs.

The benchmark uses deterministic synthetic face crops; detection is replaced at the extraction boundary. It measures the recognition/preprocessing stage, not detection time or model accuracy, and asserts no timing threshold.

batch14.title: Keep high-dimensional embeddings usable in pgvector
batch14.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained pgvector registration fix.

## What has been done
The default VGG-Face model produces 4,096-dimensional embeddings, but pgvector's HNSW index for the `vector` type supports at most 2,000 dimensions. Initialization currently tries to create that index unconditionally, so registration and even an empty-gallery search fail with `column cannot have more than 2000 dimensions for hnsw index`.

Create the table with its full embedding dimensions and skip only the unsupported HNSW index above that limit. Log that these galleries use an exact scan. Models at or below 2,000 dimensions keep their existing HNSW indexes and distance operators. The vectors are not truncated or quantized.

The limit is documented in [pgvector's HNSW support](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector#hnsw).

## How to test
[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43862495314), Python 3.10 and 3.12, real PostgreSQL 16.16 and pgvector extension 0.8.7:
- Original production source: 8 failing regression cases and 5 passing controls.
- Patched source plus existing datastore and connection-ownership regressions: 52 passed in each environment.
- Pylint 2.15.10: 10.00/10; MyPy 1.14.1: 145 source files passed; test formatting passed.

The integration tests exercise 128, 2,000, 2,001, and 4,096 dimensions with both distance operators; inspect actual index definitions; check stored vector dimensions and values through SQL; compare returned nearest neighbors and distances; and cover the public registration path, empty galleries, and invalid column dimensions.

Recognition is replaced at the embedding/metadata boundary. PostgreSQL schema creation, storage, index creation, and searches use the actual driver and database. The high-dimensional fallback is exact scanning and can be slower than indexed search on a large gallery.

batch16.title: Decode embeddings returned by pgvector Python 0.5
batch16.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained pgvector driver compatibility fix.

## What has been done
pgvector Python 0.5 changed Psycopg's decoded `vector` value from a NumPy array to a `Vector` object. That object is not iterable, so the existing `list(value)` calls raise `TypeError: 'Vector' object is not iterable`. This breaks single-identity reads, full-gallery reads, exact searches, and identification with the current driver.

Use the driver's `to_list()` method when available and retain the existing conversion for older array-returning drivers. The production change is two return-value conversions.

The driver change is recorded in [pgvector Python's 0.5.0 changelog](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector-python/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md).

## How to test
[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43862864470), using real PostgreSQL 16.16, pgvector extension 0.8.7, and Psycopg 3.3.9:
- Python 3.12 / pgvector Python 0.5.1: original source has 8 failures and 3 passing controls; patched source plus adjacent regressions has 50 passes.
- Python 3.10 / pgvector Python 0.4.2: all 11 new cases already pass on the original source, and all 50 selected cases pass after the change.
- Repository-pinned Pylint: 10.00/10; MyPy: 145 source files passed; test formatting passed.

The tests read actual database values through both decoder generations, verify single-row and streamed batch results, exercise public exact search and identification, and preserve missing-identity, empty-gallery, and native ANN-search behavior. Recognition is replaced at the embedding boundary; database reads, decoded values, and distance calculations are real.
